title: Kelly Bet Size

statement.md: The Kelly criterion gives the fraction of bankroll to bet on a favourable wager: a bet wins $b$ dollars per dollar staked with probability $p$, and loses the stake with probability $q = 1-p$. The growth-optimal fraction is
When the edge is negative the formula returns a negative number; in that case the correct action is to bet nothing, so report $0$. Compute the Kelly fraction for each query.

inputFormat: First line: $t$ ($1 \le t \le 10^5$). Then $t$ lines with two numbers $p$ and $b$ ($0 \le p \le 1$, $0 < b \le 1000$).
outputFormat: For each query, the Kelly fraction clamped below at zero, rounded to the nearest value with exactly 4 decimal places. The tests never put the exact value of $f^*$ within $10^{-9}$ of a halfway point between two 4-decimal values, so any correct computation (exact decimals or doubles) prints the same digits.
constraints: The exact value of $f^{*}$ (computed from the decimal inputs as written) is never within $10^{-9}$ of a rounding halfway point at the fourth decimal, so tie-breaking rules such as half-up or half-even never matter and double precision is enough.
hints: The clamp at zero is part of the specification, not an afterthought.
Print with exactly four decimals, string formatting, not rounding by eye.
editorial: [{"type": "p", "md": "Direct evaluation of $f^* = (bp - q)/b$ with a max(0, ·) clamp. The mathematical interest is in the reading: $f^*$ is the edge divided by the odds, numerator $bp - q$ is expected profit per unit staked, denominator $b$ normalises by the payoff. A 60/50 coin at even money says bet 20% of bankroll; the same coin at 2:1 says 25%, better prices raise size sublinearly, which is why practitioners bet *fractional* Kelly (half or quarter) to damp variance."}]

solutions.python:
import sys


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    t = int(data[0])
    out = []
    for i in range(t):
        p = float(data[1 + 2 * i])
        b = float(data[2 + 2 * i])
        q = 1.0 - p
        f = (b * p - q) / b
        if f <= 0:
            f = 0.0
        out.append(f"{f:.4f}")
    print('\n'.join(out))


main()
